cards.a: Cloud-like infrastructure (self-service, elastic, metered) that runs on dedicated, on-premises resources, e.g. VMware or OpenStack under your control. It keeps data and compliance in-house but adds capex and operational cost.

cards.q: What are the defining characteristics of a private cloud?
cards.a: Owned by your organization, located on-prem or dedicated, dedicated tenancy, and full control. It is the cloud model on your own hardware.

cards.q: How are cloud features delivered locally in a private cloud?
cards.a: Self-service via a portal, elasticity from hypervisor resource pools, metering via usage tracking, and orchestration through tools like vRealize or OpenStack.

cards.q: What platforms build a private cloud?
cards.a: VMware vSphere (most common), OpenStack (open source), Nutanix (hyperconverged), and Azure Stack (hybrid).

cards.q: Compare private versus public cloud on cost, control, compliance, and scale.
cards.a: Private: capex cost, full control, easier compliance, limited scale. Public: opex cost, limited control, shared compliance, elastic scale.

cards.q: When does a private cloud win over public?
cards.a: For regulated data (compliance), latency-sensitive local workloads, legacy integration, and cost control under steady load. Sensitive and steady workloads stay on-prem.

cards.q: What networking options does a private cloud use?
cards.a: Virtual switches (vSwitch), VLANs for segmentation, NSX for SDN overlays, and internal east-west traffic.

cards.q: What commands inspect private cloud networking on ESXi?
cards.a: esxcli network vswitch standard list shows vSwitches and esxcli network ip interface list shows IP interfaces; otherwise use platform consoles/APIs.

cards.q: VMs in a private cloud have no network. What do you check?
cards.a: Check the vSwitch and its portgroups, then VLAN/portgroup isolation, host capacity/pools, and storage (datastore) for slowness.

cards.q: Which platforms are the classic private-cloud stacks?
cards.a: VMware and OpenStack; Azure Stack serves as the hybrid option.

cards.q: Match the quick review: owner, tenancy, cost, control, platform, compliance, scale, network.
cards.a: Owner = you; tenancy = dedicated; cost = capex; control = full; platform = VMware/OpenStack; compliance = easier; scale = limited; network = vSwitch/NSX.
